avs8nmg5bfieddedufn1ermbrf.value: Credits: conjugation, f⁻¹ ∘ g ∘ f, is standard group theory, and going to another space, acting and coming back, as a Rubik's cube commutator does, is Ersagun's idea for this language (influence). The 2.2 power is the simple form of sRGB's curve (IEC 61966-2-1), and doubling light in linear light is standard colour practice (textbook). The band split is the Haar wavelet (Alfréd Haar, 1910) (prior art). The page is ours.

bdb5gan4dkot9m1ag2h7b0m475.value: Some changes are easy in another space. Move there, make the change, move back: f⁻¹ ∘ g ∘ f, as a Rubik's cube move turns a corner into place, twists it and turns it back. Here conjugate(f, g) does that, and f⁻¹ is f run backwards, written nowhere.
